No good deeds on other days surpass those of the first ten days of Dhul Hijja, not even jihad, unless one risks life and property and returns with neither.
Asked on the way from Mina to Arafat how Talbiya was said with the Prophet, Anas said people said Talbiya and Takbir, and neither was objected to.
On Eid women, even virgins and menstruating women, were ordered out to say Takbir behind the men; a spear was the Prophet's sutra, and he told women to give alms.
Going towards Al-Baqi on Eid al-Adha the Prophet said prayer comes before sacrifice, an animal slaughtered earlier is no sacrifice, and allowed one man a young goat for himself alone.
After the Eid prayer and sermon the Prophet, with Bilal, preached to the women, who gave rings as alms; all women were ordered out, menstruating ones keeping from the musalla.
The Prophet slaughtered at the musalla; whoever slaughtered before the prayer was to slaughter again, others in Allah's name, and one man alone was allowed a young goat.
On Eid the Prophet returned by another way and prayed only two rak'at; he let girls beat tambourines in the days of Eid and Mina, and Aisha watch a display.
Night prayer is offered two rak'at at a time and closed with one rak'a of witr, as the Prophet did before Fajr's two rak'at; three-rak'at witr was also seen.
The Prophet prayed witr at various hours of the night, woke Aisha to pray it, told people to make it their last night prayer, and prayed it on his mount.
Qunut was recited in Fajr and Maghrib; for a month the Prophet recited it after bowing, invoking Allah against tribes who, despite a treaty, killed about seventy men he sent.
The Prophet went out to offer the prayer for rain and turned his cloak inside out.
Rising from the last bowing, the Prophet asked Allah to save named weak believers, send famine years on Mudar like Joseph's, forgive Ghifar and save Aslam.
When people refused Islam the Prophet prayed for famine years like Joseph's; hunger made them see smoke, Abu Sufyan asked him to pray for them, and verses 44:10-16 came down.
Ibn Umar recalled Abu Talib's verse watching the Prophet's rain prayer; Umar asked Al-Abbas to pray for rain; the Prophet faced the Qibla, reversed his cloak and prayed two rak'at.
Asked during the Friday sermon, the Prophet raised his hands and prayed for rain; it rained a week until he asked that it fall around them, not on them.
The rain prayer was held outside without pulpit, adhan or iqama: the Prophet faced the Qibla, invoked Allah, turned his cloak inside out and prayed two rak'at aloud.
The Prophet raised his hands high asking for rain, the people with him; seeing rain he asked for a fruitful rain, and prayed it away when excessive.
A strong wind brought anxiety to the Prophet's face, and he said he was granted victory with the wind As-Saba while 'Ad were destroyed by the westerly wind.
The Hour will not come until knowledge is taken away, earthquakes become frequent, time passes quickly, afflictions and killing increase and wealth overflows.
Asked twice to bless Najd too, the Prophet blessed only Sham and Yemen, saying earthquakes and afflictions would appear there and the side of Satan's head come from there.
After a night of rain at Al-Hudaibiya the Prophet said Allah declares that whoever credits rain to His blessing believes in Him, and whoever credits a star disbelieves in Him.
The keys of the unseen are five, known only to Allah: what tomorrow brings, what is in the womb, what one will gain, where one dies, and when rain falls.
When the sun eclipsed, as when his son Ibrahim died, the Prophet said sun and moon eclipse for no one's death or birth, and called for prayer and invocation.
The Prophet led a congregational eclipse prayer, standing and bowing long twice each rak'a, then said eclipses are Allah's signs to frighten His slaves, calling for remembrance, prayer and charity.
Asked by Aisha about punishment in the grave, which a Jewish woman had mentioned, the Prophet sought refuge from it, and after an eclipse prayer ordered people to seek refuge.
The Prophet bowed twice in each rak'a of a long eclipse prayer and said he saw Paradise, and Hell, mostly peopled by women ungrateful to husbands and good deeds.
After an eclipse prayer the Prophet said people will be tried in their graves: the believer affirms he is Allah's Messenger, the hypocrite says he does not know.
The Prophet ordered people to free slaves during the solar eclipse.
After a Jewish woman spoke of punishment in the grave the Prophet sought refuge from it, and after a long eclipse prayer ordered the people to seek refuge from it.
Sun and moon, signs of Allah, do not eclipse for anyone's death or life, as claimed at Ibrahim's death; at an eclipse hasten to pray, remember Allah and seek forgiveness.
The eclipse prayer, called in congregation and recited aloud, has four bowings and four prostrations in two rak'at; Abdullah bin Az-Zubair's two-rak'at version missed the Prophet's way.
The Prophet prostrated on reciting An-Najm, with all present but an old man who lifted earth to his forehead, and at Sad, yet not when Zaid recited An-Najm.
Abu Huraira prostrated at Al-Inshiqaq because the Prophet did, crowds prostrating with the Prophet lacked room, and Umar taught that the prostration is right but not compulsory.
The Prophet shortened prayers during a nineteen-day stay and in Mecca, and prayed two rak'at at Mina, as did Abu Bakr and Umar, while Uthman later prayed four.
The Prophet and his companions reached Mecca on the fourth of Dhul Hijja intending Hajj, and he told those without sacrificial animals to assume ihram for Umra instead.
A woman should not travel for more than three days, or in another narration a day and night, except with a mahram or her husband.
Prayers were first two rak'at and stayed so on journeys; the Prophet shortened Asr at Dhul-Hulaifa and, when hurried on a journey, prayed Maghrib together with Isha.
On journeys the Prophet prayed voluntary prayers and witr on his mount, nodding, facing wherever it went, but dismounted and faced the Qibla for the compulsory prayers.
On journeys the Prophet prayed two rak'at and no optional prayers, yet Um Hani saw him pray eight rak'at of Duha, and he prayed nawafil on his mount at night.
On journeys the Prophet combined Maghrib with Isha and Zuhr with Asr, delaying Zuhr to Asr's time if he set out before noon, with no optional prayer between them.
